_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED into src/data/index.ts. AF/G.22 population-priority push, 2026-08-13. Verified poverty-line and minimum-wage findings for 7 African countries, cross-checked against primary sources (originally leads from notes/country.docx).

reports.title: National Poverty Lines 2025 (P0310.1)
reports.description: Stats SA's annual National Poverty Lines release (P03101/P031012025.pdf, published 29 Jan 2026). KEY FINDINGS (p.3): Food poverty line R855 per person per month (May 2025 prices); Lower-bound poverty line (LBPL) R1,415 per person per month; Upper-bound poverty line (UBPL) R2,846 per person per month (Table 1, p.3). All three docx-sourced figures confirmed verbatim. Section 3 ("Adjustments to the national poverty lines," p.7) states: "Since this rebasing, Stats SA has used the CPI series to make annual price adjustments to the NPL series to ensure they are reflective of current prices" — food CPI and non-food CPI applied separately. The NPL 2023 Series is rebased on the Income and Expenditure Survey (IES) 2022/23 using the Cost-of-Basic-Needs method.

reports.title: National Minimum Wage Amendment, Government Notice No. R.7083 (Gazette No. 54075)
reports.publisher: Department of Employment and Labour (South Africa)
reports.description: Government Notice No. R.7083, Gazette No. 54075 (3 February 2026), issued by Minister Nomakhosazana Meth under the National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018. Quote: "farm workers are entitled to a minimum wage of R30,23 per hour" / "domestic workers are entitled to a minimum wage of R30,23 per hour" / "workers employed on an expanded public works programme are entitled to a minimum wage of R16,62 per hour". Effective 1 March 2026; increase from the prior rate of R28.79/hour (GN 52053, 4 Feb 2025), confirmed via the companion Department of Employment and Labour media statement (03 Feb 2026): "a rise in the National Minimum Wage (NMW) rates for 2026 from R28,79 to R30,23 for each ordinary hour worked". Cite the gazette PDF directly, not the gov.za landing page, which carries no extractable body text.

reports.title: The Kenya Poverty Report 2022
reports.description: KNBS's 2022 poverty report (Sections 2.2.1 "The Food Poverty Line", 2.2.2 "The Overall Poverty Line", p.15; Section 6.1 Conclusion). Quote: "The resulting food poverty lines were KSh 2,668 and KSh 3,521 for rural and urban areas, respectively." / "The overall poverty lines in monthly adult equivalent terms were calculated as KSh 4,358 and KSh 8,006 for rural and urban areas, respectively." / "The national food poverty headcount rate for individuals in 2022 was 31.7 per cent" / "The overall poverty rate increased slightly from 37.3 per cent in 2021 to 39.8 per cent in 2022". NOTE — CORRECTED FIGURE: the underlying research lead (docx) mis-transcribed the urban food poverty line as KSh 3,251; the verified primary figure is KSh 3,521 (digit transposition in the original lead, corrected here). The overall poverty line's non-food component is updated using the non-food Consumer Price Index (CPI); the food component is updated via Kenya Continuous Household Survey (KCHS) unit-value prices, not CPI.

reports.title: 2017/18 Household Budget Survey — Key Indicators Report
reports.description: NBS's 2017/18 Household Budget Survey (HBS) Key Indicators Report, still the most current national poverty line as of this verification round (the 2024-25 Integrated Household Budget Survey remains in pilot stage as of a 27 Jan 2025 Pilot Survey Report; no full results published yet). Quote: "Food Poverty Line: TZS 33,748 per adult equivalent per month" / "Basic Needs Poverty Line: TZS 49,320 per adult equivalent per month". Methodology: "the monetary value of minimum food bundle or basket containing 2,200 kilocalories per adult per day for one month... based on the food consumed by 10 to 50 percent of the population," derived from "251 most common food items." No CPI-indexation language found in this report; poverty lines are updated via periodic HBS re-survey, not an annual CPI-adjustment formula.

reports.title: The Labour Institutions (Minimum Wage for Private Sector) Order, 2025 (Government Notice No. 605A)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability, Tanzania
reports.description: New finding, not present in the original research leads. Government Notice No. 605A, sector-specific private-sector minimum wages, in force "on the 1st day of January, 2026" and superseding the 2022 minimum wage order. Example sector rates: agricultural sector (crop/animal production) TZS 175,000/month; domestic workers (residing) TZS 80,000/month; commercial banks TZS 733,000/month. Rates are set per-sector (16 sectors) rather than as a single national figure. No CPI-indexation language found — set by periodic ministerial order, the same model as the poverty line.

reports.title: Ghana Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Report, 2024/2025 Q3
reports.description: GSS-authored MPI report (06-2024-2025Q3-MPI-Report, signed, published Jan 2026). Quote: "Ghana has experienced a continuous reduction in its monetary poverty over 25 years from 51.7 percent in 1991/1992 to 23.4 percent in 2016/2017." Multidimensional poverty rate for Q3 2025: 21.9% (~7.2 million people), down from 24.9% in Q4 2024. The 23.4% monetary poverty rate (GLSS7, 2016/17) is confirmed and matches the original research lead's comparison table. NOTE: the original lead's specific GH¢792-982 (extreme) and GH¢1,314-1,760 (upper) monetary poverty-line cedi figures could NOT be independently verified against this or any other primary GSS document and are deliberately excluded from this node — see _dropped. No CPI-indexation statement found for the poverty line; GSS uses a periodic Ghana Living Standards Survey (GLSS) model, similar to Tanzania's HBS model.

reports.title: National Daily Minimum Wage 2026 Announcement
reports.publisher: Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (Ghana), with Ministry of Finance / National Tripartite Committee
reports.description: New finding, not present in the original research leads. New minimum wage set at GH₵21.77/day, effective 1 Jan-31 Dec 2026, a 9% increase from GH₵19.97. The Finance Minister made a contextual remark that "the country has gone through difficult times with high inflation and interest rates," but this was descriptive context, not a stated indexation formula — inflation is referenced, not formulaic, for this wage-setting decision.

reports.title: CAPMAS Poverty Rates in Egypt Decline to 29.7% (HIECS 2019/20)
reports.publisher: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS), via State Information Service (SIS)
reports.description: CAPMAS-sourced poverty rate, published via SIS (official government portal), announced December 2020 and based on the Household Income, Expenditure and Consumption Survey (HIECS) 2019/20. Egypt's national poverty rate is cited as 29.7%. This is the verified, primary CAPMAS-attributable poverty figure. NOTE: an alternative 33.5% figure attributed in the original research lead to "HIECS 2021-22 / CAPMAS" could NOT be confirmed as a CAPMAS-authored publication in this round — see _dropped for full detail; do not treat 33.5% as a CAPMAS-primary figure in this corpus.

reports.title: National Wages Council Raises Private-Sector Minimum Wage to EGP 7,000
reports.publisher: National Wages Council, via Ministry of International Cooperation (Egypt)
reports.description: New finding, not present in the original research leads. Quote: "The National Wages Council decided to raise the minimum wage for private sector workers to 7,000 EGP, up from 6,000 EGP; effective starting March 1, 2025." Also introduces "a minimum periodic allowance of 3% of the insurance subscription wage (minimum 250 EGP monthly)" and "the first-ever minimum hourly wage for part-time work at no less than 28 EGP." Chaired by Dr. Rania Al-Mashat (Minister of Planning, Economic Development and International Cooperation). The prior step (EGP 6,000, effective May 2024) was separately confirmed via the Ministry of Planning (mped.gov.eg). No CPI-indexation formula found; the wage is set by discretionary Council decision. Flag as current-as-of-last-confirmed-update (March 2025), not guaranteed current as of Aug 2026 — no 2026 update could be located.

reports.title: 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Survey Report
reports.description: NBS MPI report, launched 17 November 2022 in Abuja. Quote: "63% of persons living within Nigeria (133 million people) are multidimensionally poor." / "40.1% of people are poor according to the 2018/19 national monetary poverty line, and 63% are multidimensionally poor according to the National MPI 2022." All figures confirmed exactly against the original research lead. No more recent (2024/25) national poverty report was found; NBS's e-library still lists the 2019 "Poverty and Inequality in Nigeria" executive summary as its current poverty report.

reports.title: Presidency Statement: President Tinubu Approves N70,000 National Minimum Wage
reports.description: Presidential press release (State House, 18 July 2024 meeting). Quote: "no one in the federal establishment should earn less than N70,000" / "We affirm three years. We will review." (President Tinubu). N70,000 figure and 3-year statutory review cycle confirmed via this Presidency source. NOTE: the National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Act 2024's own statutory text (Sec 3(1): "Every employer shall pay a national minimum wage of not less than N70,000.00 per month"; Sec 3(4): three-year review) was only locatable via a non-government NGO host (Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre, placng.org) — per the evidence standard for this corpus that NGO-hosted copy is not treated as the primary citation and is not used as the URL here; this node cites only the Presidency statement, which independently confirms the N70,000 figure and review cycle. No CPI-indexation — the review interval is a fixed 3-year statutory cycle, not a CPI formula.

reports.title: Federal Civil Service Minimum Salary Increase, September 2025
reports.publisher: Federal Civil Service Commission, Ethiopia (via Ethiopian News Agency)
reports.description: Quote: "the minimum salary of a government employee will rise from 4,760 Birr to 6,000 Birr," effective September 2025. IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION: this is a Federal Civil Service minimum salary, applicable to government employees only — it is NOT a national or private-sector minimum wage. Multiple secondary sources independently confirm Ethiopia has no economy-wide statutory minimum wage law. This node must be labeled precisely as "Federal Civil Service minimum salary" and never as "National Minimum Wage." No CPI-indexation language found; the adjustment appears to be a discretionary Commission-set change, not an automatic formula.

dependencies.basis: Stats SA's National Poverty Lines 2025 report (Section 3, "Adjustments to the national poverty lines," p.7) states verbatim: "Since this rebasing, Stats SA has used the CPI series to make annual price adjustments to the NPL series to ensure they are reflective of current prices" — food CPI and non-food CPI are applied separately to roll the NPL series forward between IES rebasing points. This is the single most clearly evidenced CPI-linkage case across all seven countries checked this round.

_dropped.why: The Kenya Poverty Report 2022 does state a real CPI linkage — but only for the non-food component of the overall poverty line: "the non-food Consumer Price Index (CPI) was used to update the non-food allowance for the 2021 and 2022 KCHS." The food component (the larger, headline part of the poverty line — food poverty lines KSh 2,668 rural / KSh 3,521 urban) is instead updated using Kenya Continuous Household Survey (KCHS) unit-value prices, which is a distinct methodology, not labeled CPI anywhere in the source. Because a `calculated_from`/`methodology_depends_on` edge on the poverty-line node as a whole would overstate the linkage (implying the full poverty line is CPI-derived, when only the non-food sub-component is), this was deliberately left out of the dependencies array and logged here instead. If a future pass wants to model the non-food allowance as its own sub-node, a clean edge could be drawn to ke-knbs-cpi at that point.

The 2024 Kenyan minimum wage instrument (Regulation of Wages (General) (Amendment) Order, 2024, Legal Notice No. 164, dated 9 October 2024) was located and its existence/date confirmed via Kenya Law's citation page (new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/ln/2024/164), but the actual wage figures could not be extracted verbatim from any accessible primary document: kenyalaw.org's PDF returned HTTP 403 (nginx bot-block, confirmed via direct curl, not a proxy/TLS artifact), the Kenya Law AKN page is a JS-loaded PDF viewer with no extractable body text, and labour.go.ke/node/470 returned 404. Per the verbatim-quote evidence standard, no node was minted for this figure. Secondary corroboration suggests a ~12% increase to domestic worker/general minimum wages effective ~Nov 2024, but this is not primary-sourced and is not written into the corpus. CPI-linkage for the minimum wage: also NOT FOUND (text was inaccessible to check). Recommend a follow-up pass with browser-based/interactive tooling to get past the bot-gate before minting this node.

The 2017/18 HBS Key Indicators Report does not state that Tanzania's poverty lines are adjusted using CPI between survey rounds. Poverty lines are instead updated via a periodic re-survey model (a new Household Budget Survey every several years), most recently attempted via the 2024-25 Integrated Household Budget Survey (IHBS), which was still in pilot stage (Pilot Survey Report, 27 Jan 2025) with no full results published as of this check. No CPI-indexation edge is supported by the primary text; not added to dependencies.

The original research lead (docx) cited specific monetary poverty-line figures of GH¢792-982 (extreme poverty line) and GH¢1,314-1,760 (upper poverty line). These exact cedi amounts could NOT be located in any primary Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) document within available tool access this round — the GSS MPI report that was fetched and verified (gh-gss-mpi-2025q3-report) contains the 23.4% (GLSS7, 2016/17) and 21.9%/24.9% (MPI, Q3 2025/Q4 2024) rates, but not these specific cedi thresholds. Two further URLs were attempted and failed: statsghana.gov.gh/gssmain/fileUpload/pressrelease/MPI%20GHANA%20REPORT.pdf (404) and statsghana.gov.gh/publications/survey-reports (JS-rendered SPA, no static content). Per the evidence standard, these monetary-line figures are excluded from the corpus entirely rather than written into a node — only the MPI rate (verified, GSS-authored) is retained in gh-gss-mpi-2025q3-report.

No CPI-indexation statement was found for Ghana's poverty line; it follows a periodic Ghana Living Standards Survey (GLSS) re-survey model, similar to Tanzania's HBS model, rather than an annual CPI-adjustment formula. Not added as a dependency edge.

The Finance Minister's remark accompanying the 2026 daily minimum wage announcement ("The country has gone through difficult times with high inflation and interest rates") references inflation only as descriptive/contextual justification, not as a stated indexation formula or methodology. Per the instruction not to assert a CPI dependency edge unless one is explicitly confirmed as formulaic, this is deliberately excluded from dependencies and logged here as a 'referenced but not formulaic' case rather than a genuine CPI-linkage edge.

The original research lead attributed a 33.5% national poverty rate to CAPMAS, sourced to HIECS 2021/22. This attribution could NOT be confirmed against any CAPMAS-authored primary publication. The only source located for the 33.5%-for-2021 figure is a World Bank Poverty & Equity Brief (October 2025, documents1.worldbank.org) — a secondary/international-body estimate computed from HIECS 2021-22 microdata, not a CAPMAS headline announcement. A non-primary secondary news article (not evidentiary, noted only as a research lead) alleges CAPMAS has withheld official HIECS 2021/22 poverty results since a promised October 2023 release date passed without publication. capmas.gov.eg's own root page was fetched but returned only header/boilerplate with no navigable poverty-report links. CONCLUSION: do NOT write 33.5% into any node as a CAPMAS-attributed fact. The verified CAPMAS-primary figure, written into eg-capmas-poverty-rate-2019-20, is 29.7% for HIECS 2019/20 (announced December 2020).

No CPI-indexation formula was found for Egypt's minimum wage; the EGP 7,000 rate (and the prior EGP 6,000 step) were both set by discretionary National Wages Council decision, not a stated CPI-based formula. Not added as a dependency edge.

_dropped.edge: ng-presidency-nmw-70000-2024 -> [National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Act 2024 statutory text]
_dropped.why: The Act's own statutory text (Sec 3(1) and 3(4)) was only locatable via a non-government-hosted copy: placng.org (Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre), a Nigerian NGO, not a government body. Per the standing evidence rule requiring a primary/government-authored source for verbatim-quote citation, this NGO-hosted PDF is not used as the corpus citation — it served only as corroboration of the figures in the Presidency statement, which is what ng-presidency-nmw-70000-2024 cites instead. A separate attempted URL (placng.org/lawsofnigeria/print.php?sn=323) returned a stale/wrong version of the law (the 2000 Act, N5,500/month, not the 2024 amendment) — flagged as a trap for future researchers. nass.gov.ng's Acts/Bills sections were searched but the 2024 amendment was not found in visible content within the time available. Recommend a follow-up pass specifically to locate the National Assembly's or Federal Gazette's own copy of the 2024 Act before treating its statutory text (as opposed to the Presidency's confirming statement) as directly citable.

No CPI-indexation basis found for Nigeria's minimum wage; the review mechanism is a fixed 3-year statutory cycle ("We affirm three years. We will review"), not a CPI formula. Not added as a dependency edge.

No accessible, current, ESS-authored primary document could be found establishing Ethiopia's national poverty line. ess.gov.et's homepage and /households page surfaced no current poverty-line/HCES publication links (the Household Consumption and Expenditure Survey's latest listed release is 2010/11, and the Welfare Monitoring Survey's is 2011); ess.gov.et/publications is a JS-rendered SPA with no static publication list; ess.gov.et/download/2021-22-survey-report/ resolves to the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Panel Survey (ESPS-5) 2021/22, a different survey (panel/welfare dynamics) containing no poverty line or headcount figures; pdc.gov.et (Planning and Development Commission) failed to resolve via DNS entirely. The original research lead's claim of a national line 'anchored to 2,200 kcal (1996 basket)' and a ~23.5% (2015/16) poverty rate could not be independently verified against any ESS-authored primary document and is logged here as NOT FOUND rather than merged into the corpus. The lead itself only cited ESS's portal generically plus World Bank briefs, consistent with what this verification pass found.

No CPI-indexation language was found for the Federal Civil Service minimum salary increase; it appears to be a discretionary Federal Civil Service Commission-set adjustment (4,760 to 6,000 Birr, effective September 2025), not an automatic CPI-based formula. Not added as a dependency edge. Separately reiterating the scope correction: this figure applies to government employees only and must never be represented in the corpus as a 'National Minimum Wage' — Ethiopia has no economy-wide statutory minimum wage law for the private sector, per multiple independent secondary confirmations.

Unlike South Africa's poverty line, the 2026 National Minimum Wage gazette notice and the companion Department of Employment and Labour media statement do not state a CPI-based formula for the R28.79 to R30.23 increase. The National Minimum Wage Act does require the statutory Commission to consider CPI among other factors annually, but that basis is not stated in either primary document accessed this round; substantiating a calculated_from: CPI edge for the minimum wage (as opposed to the poverty line) would require the NMW Commission's own annual recommendation report, which was not part of this verification pass. Flagged as an open lead for a future round, not a confirmed edge now.
